title: Lowest Value (LOWEST)
summary: Traces the lowest value of the source over a rolling window, starting on the first bar with the lowest value seen so far.
description:
Lowest Value draws the running minimum of a price series over a fixed lookback. On each bar it looks at the last `period` values of the source and plots the smallest of them, so the line steps down the moment a new low enters the window and steps up only when the old low drops out of the back of it.

While fewer than `period` bars exist, the line is the lowest value seen since the first bar, so it starts on the very first bar instead of leaving a warmup gap. A missing source value is read as zero and still takes its place in the window. Once the window is full, the line is the plain rolling lowest of the last `period` bars, the current bar included.
howToRead:
Read the line as the floor of recent trading. A flat stretch means no new low has been made inside the window, and its length shows how long the last low has held. A step down means price has just set a new low for the window. When the line steps up, the old low has aged out, which often follows a quiet or rising market.

The window includes the current bar, so the source can never be below the line. To test for a breakdown, compare the source with the line one bar earlier. With the low as the source, the line has the shape of a simple channel stop for a long position.

settings.label: Period
settings.description: How many bars the window covers. A longer window holds old lows for longer and changes less often.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The series whose lowest value is tracked, for example the close or the low of each bar.

faq.q: Why does the line start on the first bar?
faq.a: Until the window holds `period` bars, the study reports the lowest value seen so far. After that it reports the lowest value of the last `period` bars.

faq.q: Can the source ever be below the line?
faq.a: No. The window includes the current bar, so the line is always at or below the source. Compare the source with the previous bar's value of the line to spot a new low.

faq.q: Can I use it as a trailing stop?
faq.a: Yes. With the low as the source, the line rises as old lows drop out and never falls unless price makes a new low, which is the shape of a simple channel stop for a long position.
